notes: Third sweep, at 0397dec: five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. Each result.json records skill_hash 48939e64..., which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the current idiomatic-elixir/ folder, and every transcript contains both the new public-function sentence of the with rule and the last sentence of the do: rule. All five read SKILL.md and haiku-1 also read references/library-design.md, so Expected reads is met in all five. In the scratch folder all five pass mix format --check-formatted. This machine's Hex cache has no decimal package (the previous sweep built Decimal 2.3.0 from it), so the runs were compiled with --warnings-as-errors against a stand-in Decimal written in the scratch folder. Four compile with no warning. Haiku-2 gets one type warning at line 143, which comes from the stand-in's finite?/1 always returning true. The doctests pass against the stand-in: one doctest block each in haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2; opus-1 and haiku-1 have none. A probe gave correct per-currency totals, last-order dates (including a -02:00 order that falls on the next UTC day), top-customer order and empty results for []. All five return {:error, reason} for a bad amount, an unknown status, a missing key and a bad date. Haiku-1's and haiku-2's sessions wrote their check scripts outside their run folders (scratchpad/check/run.exs and runs/order-report/check/); those files are not graded.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: "Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function". The verdict is decided by "This holds in a public function whose only fallible call is the first step and whose body builds the result: the `with` saves the error clause and costs the reader a search for steps that are not there." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 150), together with the unchanged "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." (line 118). The rule's example is now the build/1 shape. Violating runs out of 5: one-step with 0; case nested in a with body 0; else 0. All five write build/1's single parse_orders/1 call as a case with `{:error, _reason} = error -> error` (opus-1 line 60, haiku-1 50, haiku-2 63, sonnet-1 64, sonnet-2 78). All five chain the lookups and parses in one multi-step with: opus-1 has five steps at lines 127-131, and the other four have eight (haiku-1 66-73, haiku-2 114-121, sonnet-1 139-146, sonnet-2 140-147). The previous sweep had 2 of 5 (both Sonnet, in build/1), and the 2026-10-22 check batch had 0 of 4. Opus-1's parsed_field/3 (lines 151-156) chains string_field/2 into parse_text/3 inside a case branch rather than in a with. The rule governs a with, and the code writes none there, so this is held clean and not listed.

New rule, graded against its current text: "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else", decided by line 336 of idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md. This is the first sweep that grades it with Opus. Violating runs out of 5, per sentence: do: on a body of several steps 0; a case, with or comment under do: 0; a mixed function whose block clause is not set apart 0, since no function mixes do: and block clauses; do: kept when most clauses need blocks 0; a one-expression body too long for its head's line 0, since every do: line fits and passes mix format. Every function-level do: is a one-expression clause: parse_status/1 in all five, plus opus-1 reverse_orders/1 (lines 123-124), haiku-1 completed?/1 (156), haiku-2 sum_amounts/1 (95) and invalid_amount/0 (148), and sonnet-2 completed?/1 (123). The keyword form `if ..., do: ..., else: ...` (opus-1 line 174, haiku-2 line 143) is an if expression, not a function body, so it is not counted here. As in the check-2 batch, one-expression bodies written as blocks are not counted.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: "Use captures for one-call lambdas and `fn` for anything longer", decided by "and so is a capture that uses `&1` and `&2` for one operator or one call, such as `&(&1 + &2)` or `&Decimal.add(&1.amount, &2)`. When the body does more than one call, or would need `&3`, write `fn` with named arguments." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 360). Violating runs: 0 of 5. Sonnet-1 line 108 writes &Decimal.add(&1.amount, &2), which the previous sweep graded violated (its sonnet-1 line 171) under the old "would need `&2`" sentence; the new text names that exact capture as clean. The other four sum with &Decimal.add/2 after Enum.group_by/3. Haiku-2 line 100 `&{-&1.completed_count, &1.customer_id}` builds a tuple with one operator and only &1, so it is held clean. sonnet-2 line 111 `&DateTime.to_date(&1.placed_at)` is one call. Every fn destructures a tuple or names the reduce_while arguments around a case.

Unchanged rule, graded to the previous sweep's standard: "Use the `Enum` or `Map` function made for the job", decided by "a `reduce` that reads and writes one key per element is these two written by hand" (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 223). Hand-written per-key fold: 0 of 5 (previous sweep 1 of 5). All five group customers with Enum.group_by/2. Haiku-2 summarizes the groups with a for comprehension (line 71); the other four use Map.new/2. Per-currency totals use Enum.group_by/3 then Map.new/2 (opus-1 94-95, haiku-1 136-137, haiku-2 91-92, sonnet-2 105-106), or Enum.group_by/2 then Map.new/2 (sonnet-1 106-107). Completed orders are counted with Enum.frequencies_by/2 in opus-1, haiku-1 and sonnet-2; haiku-2 uses Enum.count/1 per group (line 84) and sonnet-1 Enum.count/2 per group (line 114). Both are held clean as before. The Decimal sums with Enum.reduce are reductions no table row replaces, and the reduce_while loops build lists.

Naming is unchanged and graded to the earlier standard. Violating runs per sentence, out of 5: CamelCase/snake_case 0; top-level namespace 0 (Reports.Orders and a nested Order struct); boolean functions end in ? 0 (haiku-1 and sonnet-2 define completed?/1; the others define none); get/fetch 0 (all five name the checking lookup string_field/2 and the parsers parse_*; opus-1 adds parsed_field/3 and parse_text/3); size/length 0 (not exercised); ignored values 0; domain variable names 0. As before, the earlier standard is held for text, value, code, parser, parsed, id and latest.

Other unchanged rules follow the earlier standard. Haiku-2 is the only run that catches Decimal.parse/1 failures with `_ ->` (line 144), listed under Match every expected shape; the other four match {amount, ""}, {_amount, _rest} and :error. Haiku-2's `if` inside a case branch (line 143) is listed under Keep functions short, as the 2026-10-21 grades listed a nested if or case. Its two-step pipeline on one line (line 85) is listed under the pipeline rule, as earlier sweeps listed the same shape. Opus-1's and haiku-1's build/1 @doc has no ## Examples, listed under the Comments rule. Haiku-2 prepends without reversing (line 107); nothing downstream depends on the order, so it is held clean as before. reduce_while piped into case (sonnet-1 line 79, sonnet-2 line 133) is not listed, as before. Haiku-2's last_order_at is a DateTime where the prompt asks for a date; it is not listed, as in the check-2 batch.
